title: fix(cloud): fail early on missing shipping capabilities

findings.author: claude[bot]
findings.title: [P2] correctness/quality: this only probes PR read access (GET .../pulls), but the docs (docs/notes/codex-cloud-setup.md:46-47) and PR description say
findings.body:
[P2] correctness/quality: this only probes PR **read** access (`GET .../pulls`), but the docs (docs/notes/codex-cloud-setup.md:46-47) and PR description say setup verifies "pull-request read/write access." Opening a PR or posting a review comment needs the `pull_requests: write` scope, which is a distinct GitHub permission from repo Contents and isn't exercised by this probe or by `verify_origin_write_access`. A token with Contents:write but PR:read would sail through setup and still fail later at `gh pr create`/comment time — the exact "fails only at ship time" failure mode this PR is meant to close.

Worth at minimum tightening the doc claim to "pull-request read access" if a write probe is out of scope for now.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20scripts%2Fbootstrap%2Fcodex-cloud-setup.sh%2C%20verify_github_api_capabilities()%20only%20checks%20GitHub%20pull-request%20READ%20access%2C%20but%20docs%2Fnotes%2Fcodex-cloud-setup.md%20claims%20setup%20verifies%20%22pull-request%20read%2Fwrite%20access.%22%20Either%20add%20a%20lightweight%20PR-write%20capability%20probe%2C%20or%20correct%20the%20doc%20wording%20at%20docs%2Fnotes%2Fcodex-cloud-setup.md%20lines%2046-52%20to%20say%20%22read%22%20only.%20Branch%3A%20fix%2Fcodex-cloud-capability-probes&repo=mento-protocol/monitoring-monorepo)

findings.author: claude[bot]
findings.title: [P2] quality/consistency: verifyorigingitauth (line 158-161, just above) explicitly skips its GitHub probe when origin isn't a github.com remote, to s
findings.body: [P2] quality/consistency: `verify_origin_git_auth` (line 158-161, just above) explicitly skips its GitHub probe when `origin` isn't a `github.com` remote, to support the `CODEX_CLOUD_ORIGIN_URL` override in `codex-cloud-git-helpers.sh`. Neither `verify_github_api_capabilities` nor `verify_origin_write_access` (below) carries that same guard — both call `gh repo view`/`gh api`/`git push origin` unconditionally. For a non-GitHub origin override this now hard-fails setup where it previously degraded gracefully, silently narrowing an existing escape hatch.

findings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
findings.title: Verify pull-request write access before accepting the token
findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify pull-request write access before accepting the token**

`gh api --help` states that its default method is `GET`, so this call only proves that the token can list pull requests. A token with Contents write but Pull requests read-only passes both API checks and the branch probe, then fails later when `.agents/skills/ship/SKILL.md` runs `gh pr create` or `gh pr edit`, defeating this setup change's fail-early goal. Add a non-destructive check that verifies the pull-request mutation permission.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L20-L23](https://github.com/mento-protocol/monitoring-monorepo/blob/3409e991f81053e7f42a07bb6fc8ddbd0a3598dc/AGENTS.md#L20-L23)

findings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
findings.title: Preserve the cleanup fallback after a failed deletion
findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the cleanup fallback after a failed deletion**

When the explicit branch deletion fails, setting `created=false` before returning prevents the `EXIT` trap from retrying cleanup. A transient failure therefore leaves the probe branch on the remote even though the function installs a fallback specifically for that case; keep the flag true until deletion succeeds so the trap gets one final attempt.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

findings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
findings.title: Make the temporary branch name globally unique
findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make the temporary branch name globally unique**

The seconds-resolution timestamp and `$$` do not uniquely identify a Cloud session: PID namespaces commonly reuse shell PIDs, and Bash also keeps `$$` unchanged across sibling subshells. If two setup runs overlap within one second, they can push the same probe ref; one run may reject the other's commit or delete the shared ref, causing the other run's deletion to fail even though both credentials are valid. Add a random component or use a collision-resistant temporary-ref scheme.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

findings.author: claude[bot]
findings.title: [P3] suggestion: this probe mutates the real origin repo on every setup run (creates + deletes a branch), rather than using git push --dry-run, which
findings.body: [P3] suggestion: this probe mutates the real `origin` repo on every setup run (creates + deletes a branch), rather than using `git push --dry-run`, which GitHub still authenticates and permission-checks server-side without writing the ref. That would give the same fail-early signal with no branch-creation side effect and no risk of a permanently orphaned `codex-cloud-write-probe-*` branch if the explicit delete step (line 217) fails for a reason unrelated to permissions (e.g. an org-wide signed-commit or push-protection rule). Given AGENTS.md's ADR rule for architecture decisions with a real alternative, it's worth a one-line rationale (here or in an ADR) for why the real push+delete was chosen over `--dry-run`.

findings.author: coderabbitai[bot]
findings.title: Document the distribution package source.
findings.body:
**Document the distribution package source.**

When `CODEX_CLOUD_INSTALL_PLAYWRIGHT_DEPS` is enabled, the Cloud setup runs `playwright install --with-deps chromium` and requires the apt package source. Add the Debian/Ubuntu repository or approved package proxy to the outbound-access list. Without it, fail-closed setup can stop before Chromium installs.

✅ Addressed in commit 6a65f85

findings.author: coderabbitai[bot]
findings.title: Keep cleanup enabled after a delete failure.
findings.body:
**Keep cleanup enabled after a delete failure.**

Line 218 clears `created` before the EXIT trap runs. If the first delete fails, `cleanup_probe_ref` makes no retry and the temporary branch can remain on `origin`. Keep `created=true` until deletion succeeds. Add a fixture where creation succeeds and the first delete fails.

✅ Addressed in commit 6a65f85
